## Description

**VULNERABILITY DETAILS**  

Exploitable - Exception generated by code running in the Stack starting at Unknown Symbol @ 0x000000000012f668 called from pdf!GetPDFDocInfo+0x00000000000314a5 (Hash=0x1139655b.0x230d026b)

**VERSION**  

Chrome Version: [8.0.552.224] + [stable]  

Operating System: [Win XP Pro SP3]

**REPRODUCTION CASE**  

The crash doesn't trigger every time so give it a few runs. The access violation appears to be handled so it only crashes with a debugger attached. Below is the cdb syntax I used.

C:>cdb -amsec.dll -hd -xd gp -xd bpe -o -G -c "!exploitable -v;q" C:\Documents and Settings\Administrator\Local Settings\Application Data\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe C:\fuzzed\_crasher.pdf

**FOR CRASHES, PLEASE INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONAL INFORMATION**  

Type of crash: [browser]  

Crash State: [see attached !exploitable output]

### ta...@google.com (2010-12-16)

Hey Jared, why are you using "-xd bpe"?

Chrome uses DebugBreak() (http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms679297%28v=vs.85%29.aspx) to terminate renderers in various exceptional conditions, including memory allocation failure, I suspect this will interfere with that process.

We haven't been able to reproduce an AV yet here (we'll keep trying), but your testcase does allocate lots of memory. We suspect this might just be OOM, and your debugger flags are interfering with Chrome's handling of the situation.

Can you reproduce the AV *without* ignoring DebugBreaks?

### ta...@google.com (2010-12-16)
